content: Table TABREF27 analyzes the learned tree structures. We compare similarity as measured by INLINEFORM0 against gold, left, right, and “self" trees (top), where self INLINEFORM1 score is calculated by averaging over all 6 pairs obtained from 4 different runs. We find that PRPN is particularly consistent across multiple runs. We also observe that different models are better at identifying different constituent labels, as measured by label recall (Table TABREF27 , bottom). While left as future work, this naturally suggests an ensemble approach wherein the empirical probabilities of constituents (obtained by averaging the predicted binary constituent labels from the different models) are used either to supervise another model or directly as potentials in a CRF constituency parser. Finally, all models seemed to have some difficulty in identifying SBAR/VP constituents which typically span more words than NP constituents.
